html:
FESPACO, the Panafrican Film and Television Festival of Ouagadougou, is the largest film festival in Africa. It began in 1969 in Ouagadougou, the capital of Upper Volta, now Burkina Faso, and is held every two years.

It started as a small week of African films, at a time when cinemas in Africa showed almost only foreign films and African directors such as Ousmane Sembène, maker of Black Girl, struggled to reach their own audiences. Only films by African filmmakers can compete. Its top prize is the Golden Stallion of Yennenga, named after the warrior princess of Mossi legend.

The festival got strong state support, especially under Thomas Sankara in the 1980s. It became a meeting place for filmmakers, critics and buyers from across Africa and the diaspora, and a symbol of Pan-African culture. Together with the older Carthage Film Festival in Tunisia it has helped African cinema find its voice, even through Burkina Faso's coups and insecurity.
